newsitem.title: ITALY: Arafat briefs Italians leaders on Middle east.
newsitem.headline: Arafat briefs Italians leaders on Middle east.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat met Italian leaders on Friday to brief them on the outcome of the Middle East summit in Washington earlier this week, Italian officials said.

They said Arafat met Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini in Naples. Arafat had stopped in the Italian city on his way from Tunis to Paris for talks with French President Jacques Chirac.
"We had contacts last night and this morning. Arafat has said he would like to come to inform us of the outcome of the Washington meeting," a foreign ministry spokesman said earlier.
The meeting took place after a bilateral summit in Naples between Prodi and Chirac, following which the French leader returned to Paris to await Arafat.

Chirac told a news conference in Naples that France and Italy would ask a European Union summit in Dublin on Saturday to issue a call stressing Europe's will to be involved in trying to revive the faltering Middle East peace process.
Arafat took part in a Middle East peace summit with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, King Hussein of Jordan and President Bill Clinton in Washington on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Clinton called the meeting after five days of clashes between Israelis and Palestinians in which more than 70 people were killed. The violence put the future of Israeli-Palestinian peace in doubt.
No Europeans were invited to Washington for the meeting, irking governments in many European Union capitals.
